intended_object: The inflation map Inf : H¹(G/N, M^N) → H¹(G, M) in continuous group cohomology, for a topological group G, a normal subgroup N and a topological G-module M. It sends the class of a continuous 1-cocycle c on G/N with values in M^N to the class of g ↦ c(gN), seen in M. This is read off the docstring and the module documentation (the inflation-restriction sequence, Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg 1.6.7).
explanation:
The body is `explicitMap1`, the library's map on continuous H¹ induced by a compatible pair (φ, f). Here φ is the continuous quotient map G → G/N, with G/N carrying the quotient topology, and f is the inclusion M^N ↪ M. M^N is Mathlib's `FixedPoints.addSubgroup N M` with the subspace topology, and the inclusion is continuous. The compatibility condition f(φ(g)·m) = g·f(m) holds because G/N acts on M^N through representatives.

On cocycles, `cocyclesMap1` sends c to h ↦ f(c(φ h)), and coboundaries go to coboundaries. So the map is exactly the classical inflation c ↦ (g ↦ c(gN)).

The hypotheses are the natural ones for continuous cohomology: G is a topological group (no continuity of the group operations is even needed), M is a topological abelian group with a continuous G-action, and the quotient action on M^N is continuous. That last condition is carried as an instance hypothesis because the H¹ of a G/N-module needs it; it holds automatically for discrete M. No hypotheses are too restrictive.

Mathlib only has inflation for discrete group cohomology of `Rep k G`, as the first map of `groupCohomology.H1InfRes`. That is not a more general version of this continuous construction, so I give no Mathlib counterpart.
